figures.caption: Table 1: Summary of simulators for SNN and neuromorphic computing
Table 2: Standard notation used to describe the LIF neuron model in the literature.
Table 3: Notation used to describe the mathematical and computational approaches for neurons in SuperNeuroMAT.
Table 4: Notation used to describe the mathematical and computational approaches for synapses in SuperNeuroMAT.

Fig. 1: Comparison of run times of sparse and dense modes in SuperNeuroMAT for (a) 10 neurons; (b) 100 neurons; (c) 1,000 neurons; and (d) 10,000 neurons. The connection probability is shown on the X-axis, and the total run time in seconds is shown on the Y-axis.

Fig. 2: Comparison of memory consumed by the sparse and dense modes in SuperNeuroMAT for (a) 10 neurons; (b) 100 neurons; (c) 1,000 neurons; and (d) 10,000 neurons. The connection probability is shown on the X-axis, and the total memory consumed in megabytes (MB) is shown on the Y-axis.

Fig. 3: Run time comparison for SuperNeuroMAT sparse (green), SuperNeuroMAT dense (blue), NEST (orange), Brian2 (yellow), BindsNet (red), and snnTorch (purple) for (a) 10 neurons; (b) 100 neurons; (c) 1,000 neurons; and (d) 10,000 neurons. The connection probability is shown on the X-axis, and the time in seconds is shown on the Y-axis.

Fig. 4: Peak memory comparison for SuperNeuroMAT sparse (green), SuperNeuroMAT dense (blue), NEST (orange), Brian2 (yellow), BindsNet (red), and snnTorch (purple) for (a) 10 neurons; (b) 100 neurons; (c) 1,000 neurons; and (d) 10,000 neurons. The connection probability is shown on the X-axis, and the time in seconds is shown on the Y-axis.
Fig. 5: Learned weights for the Digits dataset using a two-layer SNN in SuperNeuroMAT.
Fig. 6: Confusion matrix for the Digits dataset using a two-layer SNN in SuperNeuroMAT.
Fig. 10: The graph containing eight nodes and fifteen edges used for comparing the neuromorphic shortest path algorithm implemented in SuperNeuroMAT with Dijkstra’s algorithm.

Fig. 11: 4-bit spiking adder. Takes two 4-bit operands (A and B) encoded using binary encoding as inputs, performs the addition operation through the hidden neurons (H) and computes a 5-bit output (C).
